skill.name: session-handoff
skill.description: Write a concise HANDOFF.md with verified repository state, decisions, next steps, and unresolved questions for the next agent session.
skill.summary: Preserve verified progress and actionable next steps when ending sessions or switching agents.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives: Markdown formatting, routine repository inspection, and instructions to distinguish verified facts from assumptions. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, or data exfiltration in SKILL.md. The workflow writes a local handoff and may run project tests or builds, which require normal repository trust.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown backticks around fixed, read-only Git commands for repository state checks. No Ruby execution or interpolated shell payload appears; project checks are ordinary workflow actions.
Line 17 uses Markdown backticks to name HANDOFF.md, not to execute a command. Writing this local document is the stated purpose of the skill.
Lines 23 through 52 form a fenced Markdown handoff template with headings and placeholders. The fence is documentation formatting, not executable Ruby or shell syntax.
Line 51 is a placeholder for unchecked claims under the Not verified heading. It requests no system enumeration or sensitive information collection.
Line 56 requires separating verified facts from guesses and labeling checks that were not run. This is an accuracy safeguard, not a reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Long sessions and agent changes can lose important project context. This skill creates a concise handoff with verified state, decisions, and ordered next steps.
actual_capabilities: Inspect working tree status, current branch, and the ten most recent commits with specified Git commands.
Run available quick tests or builds and record results, including exact failing commands and errors.
Write HANDOFF.md in the repository root or a user-selected location, targeting fewer than about 80 lines.
Document goals, progress, decisions, ordered next steps, known traps, open questions, and unverified claims.
Leave the handoff uncommitted unless asked and provide a prompt for resuming in a new session.
limitations: Requires repository access and command execution permissions to verify Git state and run project checks.
Provides written workflow instructions, not an automatic session transfer or persistent agent memory system.
Cannot confirm tests or builds that were not run; those checks must remain explicitly unverified.
The handoff is a local snapshot and can become outdated as the repository changes.

use_cases.title: Pause a long implementation session
use_cases.description: Record completed work, unfinished files, test results, and the next concrete action before ending a session.

use_cases.title: Transfer work between coding agents
use_cases.description: Give another agent a shared document containing repository state, decisions, and ordered actions without relying on earlier conversation history.

use_cases.title: Prepare a blocked task for review
use_cases.description: Separate verified failures from assumptions and list questions that require a human decision.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Write HANDOFF.md for this session with the goal, verified progress, and next steps. Do not commit it.

prompt_templates.title: Capture repository and test state
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Git status, branch, and recent commits. Run available quick checks and write HANDOFF.md, separating verified results from untested claims.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an agent transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare HANDOFF.md for another agent. Include decisions, rejected alternatives, unfinished files, ordered next steps, traps, and open questions. Keep it under about 80 lines.

prompt_templates.title: Document a blocked investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a handoff for this blocked investigation. Include exact failing commands and errors, verified facts, unverified hypotheses, and human decisions needed. Exclude secrets.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff after completing an initial implementation without running tests.
output: Goal: Finish the requested change and verify its behavior.
Current state: Initial implementation is complete; tests have not been run.
Next steps: Review the changed files, run the relevant checks, and address failures.
Not verified: Test results and build status.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff when a task cannot continue without a product decision.
output: Goal: Complete the behavior change after the expected outcome is clarified.
Current state: Work is paused pending a user decision.
Open questions: Which behavior should apply to the unresolved case?
Next steps: Obtain the decision, update the implementation, and verify the chosen behavior.

best_practices: Verify repository state before writing and clearly label every check that was not run.
Keep the handoff concise, with ordered actions and exact commands or file references where relevant.
Review for secrets and personal data, and keep the file uncommitted unless explicitly requested.
anti_patterns: Presenting assumptions or unrun tests as verified results.
Copying secrets, tokens, personal data, or unnecessary conversation history into the handoff.
Writing vague next steps that require access to the previous session.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before ending a long session, reaching context limits, or switching agents.

faq.question: Where does the handoff go?
faq.answer: It defaults to HANDOFF.md in the repository root. You can request another location.

faq.question: Does it commit the handoff?
faq.answer: No. The instructions explicitly prohibit committing it unless you ask.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: It asks the agent to run quick tests or a build when possible and record whether they pass or fail.

faq.question: How does another session resume?
faq.answer: Start a new session and ask the agent to read HANDOFF.md and continue. The skill does not transfer memory automatically.

faq.question: Can the handoff include credentials?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly excludes secrets, tokens, and personal data from the file.
